# Computer MCP

> A macOS computer-use MCP server with the guardrails on by default. Password
> fields are blacked out while the screenshot is still in memory, no click or
> keystroke happens until a human approves, and every call is written to an
> append-only log. No account, no API key, no model inside it. MIT.

Install: build from source (v0.1 is not published to npm yet).
`git clone https://github.com/Agent360dk/computerMCP && cd computerMCP/helper && swift build -c release && cd ../mcp-server && npm install`
Once published: `npx @agent360/computer-mcp`
Repository: https://github.com/Agent360dk/computerMCP
npm: @agent360/computer-mcp
Registry name: io.github.Agent360dk/computer-mcp
Platform: macOS 14 or later. No Windows or Linux build exists.
Licence: MIT

## What it is for

Letting an AI agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, or any MCP client)
see and operate macOS applications on the machine where the user actually
works - the case other desktop-automation servers are usually too unguarded
for, because that machine also holds passwords, keys and production terminals.

## The three guarantees

1. Redaction before write. Secure text fields (role AXSecureTextField, and
   role AXTextField with subrole AXSecureTextField for web pages) plus whole
   windows of listed password managers are painted opaque black on the bitmap
   in memory. The unredacted image is never written to disk.
2. Consent before action. Default mode `ask`: the first write opens a native
   macOS dialog naming the action. Password managers and terminals ask every
   time regardless of mode or prior approval. An unanswered dialog is a
   refusal, never an approval.
3. Audit after the fact. ~/.local/state/computer-mcp/audit.jsonl, mode 0600,
   append-only. Typed text is stored as a length plus a SHA-256 prefix, never
   in clear text.

## Modes

- CMCP_MODE=readonly - write tools are not listed at all
- CMCP_MODE=ask - default; session consent, dangerous apps always ask
- CMCP_MODE=allow - writes proceed without asking, still logged; dangerous
  apps still ask and that is not configurable

## Tools (12)

Look: computer_screenshot, computer_inspect, computer_apps, computer_windows,
computer_permissions, computer_audit
Touch: computer_click, computer_type, computer_key, computer_scroll,
computer_move, computer_activate

Deliberately absent: no shell execution, no arbitrary file access, no URL
fetching. A computer-control server with a shell inside it is remote access
under a friendlier name.

## Honest limits

- macOS only.
- Only what macOS marks as secure is redacted. A password in a plain text
  editor or a token in a terminal buffer is not marked and will not be hidden.
- Consent is not containment; after approval the agent drives the real Mac.
  For containment, use a virtual machine.
- Prompt injection stays possible; the dialogs and log make it visible, not
  impossible.
- Screenshots cover the active Space only.

## Pages

- https://computermcp.dev/ - overview, install, tools
- https://computermcp.dev/tools.html - every tool, what it takes, and which to
  reach for instead of the obvious one
- https://computermcp.dev/troubleshooting.html - the failures that look like
  bugs and are not, chiefly: a full-screen app hides every other window from
  both the accessibility API and the screenshot
- https://computermcp.dev/security.html - threat model, how each gate works,
  known limits
